key_insight: An AI-powered diagnostic and support platform enables local biomedical technicians in low-resource settings to identify, troubleshoot, and repair diagnostic equipment faster and with less reliance on manufacturer support, cutting downtime and improving patient care.
problem_solved: Widespread equipment downtime in LMICs caused by limited access to technical expertise, delayed manufacturer support, and lack of local maintenance capacity—leading to underutilized or nonfunctional diagnostic devices and compromised clinical services.
method: Multimodal diagnostic models that analyze sensor logs, error codes, and equipment photos to detect faults and suggest root causes.
Interactive decision-support workflows and step-by-step repair guidance (including AR/annotated images and technician-facing checklists) plus secure remote expert escalation.
Lightweight, privacy-aware deployment for mobile/edge devices with continuous learning pipelines to adapt models to local device variants and data scarcity.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners this work highlights building robust, interpretable models for constrained, real-world settings—emphasizing edge deployment, domain adaptation, and human-AI workflows that directly improve healthcare delivery in resource-limited contexts.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram showing data input (logs/photos) → AI diagnosis → technician guidance → remote expert loop
Before/after bar chart of equipment uptime and time-to-repair metrics
Mobile app UI mockup with annotated device image and step-by-step repair checklist
Map or icon grid showing impact across LMIC facilities (deployments / device types supported)
paper_title: Empowering Medical Equipment Sustainability in Low-Resource Settings: An AI-Powered Diagnostic and Support Platform for Biomedical Technicians
paper_authors: Bernes Lorier Atabonfack, Ahmed Tahiru Issah, Mohammed Hardi Abdul Baaki, Clemence Ingabire, Tolulope Olusuyi
